video.description:
Learn to explain how to talk about conflicts when devices sync the same data: Sync Conflict, Last Write Wins & Eventual Consistency, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Sync Conflict - A clash that happens when two devices change the same item before they sync.
Last Write Wins - A rule that settles a conflict by keeping the change with the newest time.
Eventual Consistency - A promise that all devices will show the same data after some time, though not right away.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Sync Conflict, Last Write Wins and Eventual Consistency in English?

dialogue.title: Two edits, one note
dialogue.setting: Debugging a note that changed twice

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, a user edited the same note on the phone and the iPad.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is a sync conflict. Both devices changed the item before they synced.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We can use last write wins. The change with the newest time stays.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In our code, `b` has `time` eight, so `winner` is `b`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. Last write wins is simple, but it can throw away the older edit.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the phone edit is lost?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. For notes, we might merge both texts instead. A sync conflict needs a clear rule.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Also, the iPad still shows the old text for a few seconds.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is normal. It is eventual consistency.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the devices only agree after some time?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Eventual consistency promises the same data later, not instantly.
We have a sync conflict on this note.
